_README: MAPPING SIDECAR for tools/tracker/update-tracker.ts. Machine-readable on purpose:
the hook must never infer ownership by guessing at path names.
SCHEMA
version : number    — bump when the shape changes, not when entries change.
rows[]  : { id, title, globs[], note? }
id    — the tracker ROW ID. MUST match the row ids the tracker itself uses
(the gap register's GE-01..GE-12 / GR-01..GR-18 / … vocabulary).
globs — repo-relative, forward-slash. Supports ** (any, incl. /), * (any,
excl. /), ? (one, excl. /). No braces, no extglob.
A path may belong to several rows; it is reported to each. A path in NO row
is reported under UNMAPPED — never silently dropped.
gates[] : { id, gate, evidence[], note? }
evidence — the artefact(s) a gate RUN writes its reading into. Their last
commit is treated as the gate's last recorded measurement. The hook
NEVER executes a gate; it only counts commits since that artefact
changed. If none resolve, the row renders NOT DETERMINED with the
reason — never '0', which would read as 'freshly measured'.
DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE. Two example rows only, both verified against real paths.
The full row set is the TRACKER LANE's to fill in: it owns the row ids and knows
which paths each row governs. Guessing the other ~80 mappings here would have
produced confident-looking ownership claims nobody measured — the failure mode
this repo logs most often. An unmapped path is disclosed loudly; a WRONG mapping
is invisible. So we ship two right ones and a mechanism that shouts about the rest.

gates.note: Shrink-only ratchet; the baseline json is rewritten only by --write-baseline, so its last commit IS the last recorded reading.
